title: Cross-stitch hedgehog in autumn leaves
subtitle: A hedgehog nestled in russet leaves on 14-count ivory Aida
excerpt: A hedgehog peering through a scatter of autumn leaves, stitched in earth tones and russets on 14-count ivory Aida. The design is approximately 80 by 65 stitches and finishes at about 14 by 12 cm. The spines are worked in individual back-stitches at varying angles to give a textured, lifelike effect.
sourceNotes: Original design. The European hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus) is a common British garden visitor in autumn. Spine texture technique is a standard embroidery approach for rendered fur or spines.

glossaryTerms.definition: A line stitch formed by inserting the needle behind the last exit point to create a solid, continuous line. In cross-stitch it is used for outlines, details, and lettering. Worked in one strand for fine detail, two strands for bolder outlines.

content.text: Fill the leaves first in four autumn colours. Then fill the hedgehog body as a solid base. The
spines are laid over the top in varying lengths and angles to break the flat fill.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 3787 (dark warm grey), 3032 (medium mocha), 3864 (light mocha), 3866 (very light mocha), 400 (dark rust), 976 (medium golden brown), 3852 (dark straw), 721 (medium orange-spice), 310 (black), 3865 (white)

content.text: Stitch the autumn leaves in 400, 976, 3852, and 721, working each leaf as a separate colour section. Leave gaps between leaves for the background ivory to show through at the edges.
Fill the hedgehog body under the spine area.
Stitch the spine area in 3787 as a solid fill first. The spines will be added on top; the dark fill provides depth through the spine gaps.
The snout uses 3032 and 3864; the underbelly uses 3866. The nose tip uses 310; the eye is a French knot in 310 with a 3865 highlight.
Work the spines in back-stitch over the body fill.

Using two strands of 3864, work back-stitch lines radiating outward from the spine area. Vary the length and angle of each stitch: short and steep at the head end, longer and flatter toward the back. Add a second layer of stitches in 3866 over the first to lighten the tips.
Add back-stitch detail to leaves and face.
Outline each leaf in one strand of 400 or 976 to define the shape. Add a leaf midrib line. Outline the hedgehog face in 3787.
Press face-down on a towel. Frame in a 18 × 15 cm rectangular mount or display stretched in a 20 cm oval hoop for an autumn-themed wall piece.
